findings.issue_text: P1: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) ignores all-clients grants when a per-client resource exists, causing false-negative authorization for admins granted MANAGE/VIEW on all clients

P2: Read-path side effect — hasPermission fallback calls get-resource-type-resource which is get-or-create, creating the 'Clients' resource during permission evaluation and polluting the permissions model

P2: UnsupportedOperationException reachable from live V1-era call sites (e.g., canExchangeTo, setPermissionsEnabled) via MgmtPermissions.clients(), producing HTTP 500 instead of deny/clean error; getEvaluationContext/hasGrantedPermission retain dead V1-only code

P2: AdminPermissions ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent cleanup now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, so flag-off deployments leave orphaned permission resources/policies pointing at removed clients/groups/roles
P3: getClientsWithPermission only enumerates per-client resources and ignores the all-clients type resource, causing inconsistent grant semantics between listing and single-resource checks
P3: AbstractPermissionTest.createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy cleanup lambdas call .getId() unconditionally on findByName(name), risking NPE if the policy was already removed

P2: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) in ClientPermissionsV2.java only evaluates the all-clients resource when no per-client resource exists, so a user with manage on all-clients can be denied canManage(X) when a per-client resource created by another permission exists — order-dependent authorization false negative (confidence 75)

P2: hasPermission fallback pre-check that policies exist on the all-clients resource performs no real authorization gating, and mixed specific/global resource evaluation with drifting scope sets can cause over-granting (confidence 50)

P2/P3: Removal-event cleanup (ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent) is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ being enabled, leaving orphaned stale authorization resources/policies if the feature was off during deletion or re-enabled later (confidence 75)

P3: Test testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient passes the admin's user id as the Users-type resource id in createPermission, possibly creating a permission on the wrong resource and weakening the test's assertion (confidence 50)

P1: getClientsWithPermission loads all client resources without pagination and runs a full permission evaluation per client (N+1 evaluation shape), unbounded — O(N) expensive evaluations per list-clients admin call (ClientPermissionsV2.java:~122)

P2: hasPermission(ClientModel) performs repeated store lookups plus a full permission evaluation per can* call with no caching, repeating identical work multiple times per request (ClientPermissionsV2.java:~207)

P2: hasPermission falls back to evaluating the all-clients resource when no per-client resource exists, including a policyStore.findByResource scan materializing a potentially large list just to check isEmpty(), for every client checked (ClientPermissionsV2.java:~215)
P3: resolveClient may issue two client lookups — getClientById then getClientByClientId on miss — in the per-permission resource-creation path (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:~175)

UnsupportedOperationException reachable from shared event listener during client deletion when V2 is enabled: AdminPermissions.registerListener's ClientRemovedEvent handler calls setPermissionsEnabled which V2 replaces with throw new UnsupportedOperationException, potentially turning client delete (204) into a 500 via MgmtPermissionsV2; same risk for exchangeToPermission

Feature-gating on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ skips cleanup handlers for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent entirely when disabled, so existing V1 permission data leaks (no longer cleaned on entity removal); gating should be at caller of V1-specific cleanup, not blanket around all three event types

Test utility base-class API changed incompatibly: getPermissionsResource, getScopePermissionsResource, createPermission changed from protected instance methods to static with new ManagedClient parameters, and createUserPolicy/createAllUserPermission renamed/re-signatured, breaking compile of external subclasses/callers of AbstractPermissionTest with no deprecation/shim

Possible resource-name mismatch in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String): looks up all-clients resource via resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()) instead of AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), so type-level canManage()/canView() may silently return false if resource is registered under a different name

Event-listener cleanup calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException under V2, potentially aborting entity delete transactions and leaving orphaned permission state

Nine methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, etc.) throw unchecked UnsupportedOperationException reachable from ClientPermissionEvaluator, surfacing as HTTP 500 instead of handled errors
Feature-flag guard on cleanup listener means removal events are ignored when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is disabled, leaving orphaned permission data that resurfaces if the feature is re-enabled
N+1 permission evaluation in getClientsWithPermission re-fetches realmResourceServer and runs full evaluatePermission per client, risking pathological latency on large realms
hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates only against per-client resource when it exists, denying callers granted only the all-clients permission — a behavioral inconsistency worth confirming
hasGrantedPermission lacks an isAdminSameRealm() guard unlike hasPermission overloads, making it unsafe if reused and prone to future cross-realm leakage

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates only the specific-client resource when it exists, never testing interplay of specific + all-client permissions; fallback path evaluates type resource's scopes instead of the requested scope
No test coverage for client-scope permissions (canView(ClientScopeModel)/canManageClientScopes) in V2 — ClientScopeModel overloads are untested
canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles in V2 drop the MANAGE/CONFIGURE admin-role fallback present in V1, a behavioral change with no test proving intent

ClientRemovedEvent cleanup is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag; with the feature off, stale permission resources/policies are orphaned on entity removal — no test covers cleanup either way
getClientsWithPermission is untested and returns resource names rather than client ids; no test asserts the canList-filtered client search returns correct clients
resolveClient's clientId-based resolution path and the fallback creating a resource named by a raw id for unknown clients are untested
Negative-path tests catch generic Exception; some assertions lack instanceOf(ForbiddenException) checks, masking non-authorization errors as expected denials
hasPermission(String) all-clients path evaluates the type resource's declared scopes rather than the requested scope; no test covers a scope-set mismatch scenario

P2: Triplicated permission-evaluation loop in ClientPermissionsV2 hasPermission/hasGrantedPermission variants, including guard divergence in hasGrantedPermission missing isAdminSameRealm/null-server checks and awkward Arrays.asList(scope) — extract a shared hasPermission(ResourceServer, Resource, String... scopes) helper
P2: Dead code — private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) helper in ClientPermissionsV2 is never called and will rot silently

P2: Behavior change in AdminPermissions — event listener cleanup for ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent is now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so disabling the flag or migration scenarios leave orphaned permission state uncleaned

P2: Wholesale UnsupportedOperationException overrides — 11 methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) are throw-stubs; V1 management API should be split out of the shared ClientPermissions interface
P3: Type-dispatch if/else chain in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource duplicates ResourceType registry mapping and will grow with each new resource type; use a resolver lookup keyed by type
P3: Copy/paste javadoc errors in ClientPermissionEvaluator — several void require*() methods are documented as 'Returns {@code true} if ...' although they return void/throw

P1: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) in ClientPermissionsV2 evaluates only the per-client resource when one exists, without OR-combining with the all-clients resource, so an all-clients manage/view grant can be silently denied once an orphaned per-client resource exists

P2: AdminPermissions cleanup listener (ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup) is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag, potentially leaving stale permission resources/policies orphaned on entity deletion if V2 is enabled but the V1 flag is disabled or toggled off

P2: Multiple ClientPermissionEvaluator methods in ClientPermissionsV2 throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"), so any remaining V1-era call path would produce an HTTP 500 instead of a deny decision in the authorization component

P2: getClientsWithPermission iterates type-Clients resources and adds resource names to the result, so the all-clients sentinel resource name can be mixed into the set of client ids, causing callers that use the set as client ids to misbehave
P3: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is a private, never-called dead helper with stale V1 token-exchange-era attribute wiring; should be removed

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) ignores all-clients grants when a per-client resource exists, causing false-negative authorization for admins granted MANAGE/VIEW on all clients

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the code first looks up a per-client Resource by name (client.getId()). It only falls back to evaluating the all-clients resource (AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) when the per-client resource is null. If a per-client resource exists but does not grant the requested scope, the method returns false without also evaluating the all-clients grant, producing a false-negative even when the caller has MANAGE/VIEW on all clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Read-path side effect — hasPermission fallback calls get-resource-type-resource which is get-or-create, creating the 'Clients' resource during permission evaluation and polluting the permissions model

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` when a per-client resource is missing, but the diff does not include `getResourceTypeResource`’s implementation nor evidence that it is a get-or-create method with side effects. Therefore the claim that this read-path call *creates* the 'Clients' resource and pollutes the model is not verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: UnsupportedOperationException reachable from live V1-era call sites (e.g., canExchangeTo, setPermissionsEnabled) via MgmtPermissions.clients(), producing HTTP 500 instead of deny/clean error; getEvaluationContext/hasGrantedPermission retain dead V1-only code

P2: AdminPermissions ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent cleanup now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, so flag-off deployments leave orphaned permission resources/policies pointing at removed clients/groups/roles
P3: getClientsWithPermission only enumerates per-client resources and ignores the all-clients type resource, causing inconsistent grant semantics between listing and single-resource checks

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the code enumerates resources by type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` and, when a permission is granted, adds `resource.getName()` to the returned set. However, single-client checks (`hasPermission(ClientModel client, ...)`) explicitly fall back to evaluating the special “all-clients” resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` when no per-client resource exists. `getClientsWithPermission` does not perform any such fallback/expansion: if only the all-clients resource exists (or the caller has only all-clients permissions), this method will at best return a set containing the name of that type resource (likely "Clients") rather than actual client ids, leading to inconsistent semantics between per-client checks and this listing method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: AbstractPermissionTest.createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy cleanup lambdas call .getId() unconditionally on findByName(name), risking NPE if the policy was already removed

adjudication.rationale: In AbstractPermissionTest, the new helpers createUserPolicy/createClientPolicy register cleanup lambdas that do `...findByName(name).getId()` without a null-check (e.g., `r.clients().get(client.getId()).authorization().policies().user().findByName(name).getId();`). If the policy was deleted earlier in the test (or by another cleanup), `findByName(name)` can return null, causing an NPE during cleanup. This risk is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) in ClientPermissionsV2.java only evaluates the all-clients resource when no per-client resource exists, so a user with manage on all-clients can be denied canManage(X) when a per-client resource created by another permission exists — order-dependent authorization false negative (confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the code first looks up a per-client Resource by name (client.getId()). If it exists, it evaluates permissions only against that resource and never considers the "all-clients" resource-type resource. The fallback to the all-clients resource (AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) happens only when the per-client resource is null. This contradicts the documented intent on ClientPermissionEvaluator.canManage(ClientModel) ("For V2 only: ... permission to MANAGE all clients") and can cause a caller with MANAGE on all clients to be denied for a specific client merely because some per-client resource exists with policies not granting them access (shadowing/false negative).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: hasPermission fallback pre-check that policies exist on the all-clients resource performs no real authorization gating, and mixed specific/global resource evaluation with drifting scope sets can cause over-granting (confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, the fallback to the all-clients resource only happens when the per-client resource is missing, and the subsequent authorization decision is still based on `root.evaluatePermission(...)` plus an explicit check that the returned permission contains the *requested* scope (`if (expectedScopes.contains(s)) return true;`). The intermediate `policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty()` check is just an optimization to avoid evaluating when no policies exist; it does not itself grant anything. The diff does not show any “mixed specific/global evaluation” leading to over-granting or “drifting scope sets” causing unauthorized scopes to be accepted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2/P3: Removal-event cleanup (ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent) is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ being enabled, leaving orphaned stale authorization resources/policies if the feature was off during deletion or re-enabled later (confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), the removal-event handling for RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, and GroupRemovedEvent is now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). Previously, these events always called `management(...).<type>().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`. With the new gating, if the feature is disabled at deletion time, the cleanup/disable step will not run, which can leave previously-created admin authorization resources/policies enabled/stale for deleted roles/clients/groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Test testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient passes the admin's user id as the Users-type resource id in createPermission, possibly creating a permission on the wrong resource and weakening the test's assertion (confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest#testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, the test later executes role-mapping against the *same* user id: `users().get(myadmin.getId()).roles().clientLevel(myclient.getId()).add(...)`. Therefore creating the Users-type permission with `resourceId = myadmin.getId()` (`createPermission(client, myadmin.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE, Set.of(MAP_ROLES), ...)`) matches the resource being acted upon and does not indicate a permission created on the wrong user/resource. The diff does not show a mismatch that would weaken the test assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: getClientsWithPermission loads all client resources without pagination and runs a full permission evaluation per client (N+1 evaluation shape), unbounded — O(N) expensive evaluations per list-clients admin call (ClientPermissionsV2.java:~122)

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(String) the code iterates over all resources of type CLIENTS via resourceStore.findByType(..., callback) and, for each resource, calls hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope), which performs a full root.evaluatePermission(...) evaluation. The diff shows no pagination/limit and a per-resource evaluation loop, so the O(N) / N+1-shaped cost is real. However, the diff does not prove this method is invoked on every list-clients admin call, so this is best classified as a performance/architecture concern rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: hasPermission(ClientModel) performs repeated store lookups plus a full permission evaluation per can* call with no caching, repeating identical work multiple times per request (ClientPermissionsV2.java:~207)

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2, most can* methods delegate to hasPermission(ClientModel,String) (e.g., canManage/client, canConfigure, canView, canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, canMapClientScopeRoles). hasPermission performs resourceStore.findByName(...) and may also load the all-clients resource plus policyStore.findByResource(...), then calls root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...)) and iterates returned permissions. There is no caching/memoization in ClientPermissionsV2, so multiple can* checks on the same client within a single flow will repeat the same store lookups and full permission evaluation, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff (not a correctness defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: hasPermission falls back to evaluating the all-clients resource when no per-client resource exists, including a policyStore.findByResource scan materializing a potentially large list just to check isEmpty(), for every client checked (ClientPermissionsV2.java:~215)

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel,String), when no per-client resource exists (resourceStore.findByName(...) == null), it falls back to the all-clients resource and then calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty() to decide whether to evaluate. This is an extra store query on that fallback path and (depending on PolicyStore API behavior) may materialize a full collection just to check emptiness, and it happens on every permission check for clients without a dedicated resource. That’s a concrete perf/architecture concern introduced by this diff, not a functional defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: resolveClient may issue two client lookups — getClientById then getClientByClientId on miss — in the per-permission resource-creation path (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:~175)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `resolveClient()` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires it into `getOrCreateResource(...)` for the new `CLIENTS` resource type. `resolveClient()` does exactly two lookups on a miss: `session.clients().getClientById(realm, id)` and, if null, `session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id)`. Since `getOrCreateResource` is part of the resource resolution/creation path used when handling permissions, this is a real, diff-grounded potential performance concern (extra DB/cache hit), but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UnsupportedOperationException reachable from shared event listener during client deletion when V2 is enabled: AdminPermissions.registerListener's ClientRemovedEvent handler calls setPermissionsEnabled which V2 replaces with throw new UnsupportedOperationException, potentially turning client delete (204) into a 500 via MgmtPermissionsV2; same risk for exchangeToPermission

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(...) to unconditionally throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). If the V2 permission management is used under this feature flag, a client deletion event will trigger this call path and can raise an unchecked exception during event handling (potentially surfacing as a 500). The mention of exchangeToPermission being reachable from this listener is not shown in the diff, but the setPermissionsEnabled path is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-gating on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ skips cleanup handlers for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent entirely when disabled, so existing V1 permission data leaks (no longer cleaned on entity removal); gating should be at caller of V1-specific cleanup, not blanket around all three event types

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, the PR wraps *all* cleanup logic for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). This is a functional change from the previous code which always executed these handlers. With the new guard, when the feature flag is disabled at runtime, entity removals will no longer call `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, so any existing fine-grained authz artifacts tied to removed roles/clients/groups will not be cleaned up on removal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test utility base-class API changed incompatibly: getPermissionsResource, getScopePermissionsResource, createPermission changed from protected instance methods to static with new ManagedClient parameters, and createUserPolicy/createAllUserPermission renamed/re-signatured, breaking compile of external subclasses/callers of AbstractPermissionTest with no deprecation/shim

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a source-incompatible API change in the public test base class `AbstractPermissionTest`: `getPermissionsResource`, `getScopePermissionsResource`, and `createPermission` were changed from protected instance methods to `protected static` methods requiring a `ManagedClient` parameter, and new helper methods like `createUserPolicy(...)`/`createAllPermission(...)` were introduced while prior per-test helpers were removed/migrated (e.g., `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest` deletes its local `createAllUserPermission`/`createUserPermission` and switches to the new base helpers). There are no deprecated instance wrappers/shims, so any subclasses/callers not updated would break at compile time. Within this diff, call sites are updated, so it’s not a runtime defect, but it is a compatibility/maintainability concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for client-scope permissions (canView(ClientScopeModel)/canManageClientScopes) in V2 — ClientScopeModel overloads are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new V2-specific authorization logic for client scopes in `ClientPermissionsV2`, notably `canManageClientScopes()`, `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` (delegates to `canManageClientScopes()`), and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` (checks `VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS` roles or `hasPermission(VIEW|MANAGE)`). The new/updated tests in `PermissionClientTest` exercise client-level operations (view/update client, secrets, default/optional client scopes changes) but do not directly cover the client-scope permission paths (e.g., authorization decisions based on `canView(ClientScopeModel)` / `canManageClientScopes()` semantics). There is no test that sets only VIEW/MANAGE permissions and then exercises client-scope listing/management in a way that specifically validates these ClientScopeModel overload checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles in V2 drop the MANAGE/CONFIGURE admin-role fallback present in V1, a behavioral change with no test proving intent

adjudication.rationale: adjudicate-error: APIConnectionError: Connection error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientRemovedEvent cleanup is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag; with the feature off, stale permission resources/policies are orphaned on entity removal — no test covers cleanup either way

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now wraps all removal-event handling (including `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent`) inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`, whereas previously the cleanup ran unconditionally. From the diff alone, it’s not provable that this creates orphaned/stale permission resources/policies in real deployments (depends on whether such artifacts can exist when the feature is off or feature toggling is supported), but it is a concrete behavioral change that could leave previously-created permission state uncleaned when the feature flag is disabled. The added/modified tests focus on permission evaluation and API behavior; none exercise the removal-event cleanup path with the feature enabled/disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission is untested and returns resource names rather than client ids; no test asserts the canList-filtered client search returns correct clients
resolveClient's clientId-based resolution path and the fallback creating a resource named by a raw id for unknown clients are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial resolution logic for client resources in `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient(...)`, which first tries `getClientById(realm, id)` and then falls back to `getClientByClientId(realm, id)`. The new tests in `PermissionClientTest`/`AbstractPermissionTest` create client permissions using `myclient.getId()` (UUID) as the resource identifier, so they only exercise the `getClientById` path, not the `clientId`-based fallback. The claim about a further fallback that creates a resource named by a raw id for unknown clients cannot be verified from the shown diff because the body after `if (name == null) {` in `getOrCreateResource(...)` is not included.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative-path tests catch generic Exception; some assertions lack instanceOf(ForbiddenException) checks, masking non-authorization errors as expected denials

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the newly added/modified negative-path tests that catch exceptions (e.g., in PermissionClientTest: testManageOnlyOneClient/testConfigureOnlyOneClient/testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient) do catch a generic Exception, but they consistently assert `instanceOf(ForbiddenException.class)` in the catch blocks. Other denial paths assert HTTP 403 via `Response` status checks rather than exceptions. The claim that “some assertions lack instanceOf(ForbiddenException) checks” is not supported by the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(String) all-clients path evaluates the type resource's declared scopes rather than the requested scope; no test covers a scope-set mismatch scenario

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String scope), the code evaluates a ResourcePermission using `resource.getScopes()` but then explicitly checks the evaluated permissions’ returned scopes against the single requested `scope` (`expectedScopes` contains only that scope). So it is not “evaluating the type resource’s declared scopes rather than the requested scope” in a way that would cause an incorrect authorization decision based on the diff alone. The test-coverage claim about a “scope-set mismatch scenario” is also not concretely tied to a demonstrated defect in the shown code paths (tests do cover all-clients permissions via `createAllPermission(..., Set.of(MANAGE))` / `Set.of(VIEW)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Triplicated permission-evaluation loop in ClientPermissionsV2 hasPermission/hasGrantedPermission variants, including guard divergence in hasGrantedPermission missing isAdminSameRealm/null-server checks and awkward Arrays.asList(scope) — extract a shared hasPermission(ResourceServer, Resource, String... scopes) helper

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` file, the permission-evaluation logic is repeated across `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)` (all iterate over `root.evaluatePermission(... )` results and compare scopes). Also, `hasGrantedPermission` does not perform the same guards (`root.isAdminSameRealm()` / `server == null`) that the two `hasPermission` overloads do, even though its current caller (`getClientsWithPermission`) does those checks beforehand. This isn’t a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff (current call path is guarded), but it is a concrete maintainability/consistency issue introduced by the change and the suggested extraction into a shared helper is actionable. The `Arrays.asList(scope)` for a single value is also visible awkwardness in both `hasPermission` methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Dead code — private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) helper in ClientPermissionsV2 is never called and will rot silently
matched_golden_ids: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point out that the private method getEvaluationContext in ClientPermissionsV2 is defined but never used (dead code) and should be removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Behavior change in AdminPermissions — event listener cleanup for ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent is now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so disabling the flag or migration scenarios leave orphaned permission state uncleaned

P2: Wholesale UnsupportedOperationException overrides — 11 methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) are throw-stubs; V1 management API should be split out of the shared ClientPermissions interface

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces `ClientPermissionsV2` with many overridden methods that unconditionally `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRoles*Permission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns this V2 implementation, so any shared code path expecting these capabilities via the common `ClientPermissions`/`ClientPermissionEvaluator` contract could hit runtime exceptions. The finding’s suggested refactor (split V1 management API out of the shared interface) is an architecture/contract concern grounded in the diff. However, the diff alone does not prove these methods are invoked under V2, so it’s not a verifiable functional bug from the patch by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Type-dispatch if/else chain in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource duplicates ResourceType registry mapping and will grow with each new resource type; use a resolver lookup keyed by type

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, the diff adds another branch `else if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType)) { name = resolveClient(session, id); }` alongside the existing USERS branch. At the same time, resource types are already centrally registered via `super(Map.of(USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE, USERS, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, CLIENTS))`. This hard-coded if/else type dispatch will need to be extended for each new ResourceType added to the registry, duplicating the mapping knowledge and creating a growing maintenance hotspot. This is an architectural/maintainability concern, not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Copy/paste javadoc errors in ClientPermissionEvaluator — several void require*() methods are documented as 'Returns {@code true} if ...' although they return void/throw

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show Javadoc inconsistencies in `ClientPermissionEvaluator` where some `void require*()` methods are described as “Returns {@code true} ...” (e.g., `void requireView();` and `void requireViewClientScopes();`). However, this is a documentation/style nit only and does not indicate a behavioral defect introduced by the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) in ClientPermissionsV2 evaluates only the per-client resource when one exists, without OR-combining with the all-clients resource, so an all-clients manage/view grant can be silently denied once an orphaned per-client resource exists

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code first looks up a per-client resource (`resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`). Only if that resource is `null` does it fall back to the all-clients resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`). If a per-client resource exists but does not grant the requested scope (e.g., an orphaned/stale resource with no policies, or policies that don't include the scope), the method never evaluates the all-clients resource, so a realm-wide grant on the all-clients resource can be denied. This contradicts the intended behavior documented in the interface comments (e.g., “permission to MANAGE all clients”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: AdminPermissions cleanup listener (ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup) is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag, potentially leaving stale permission resources/policies orphaned on entity deletion if V2 is enabled but the V1 flag is disabled or toggled off
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that the AdminPermissions cleanup listener for client/role/group removals is gated on the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) flag, which can prevent cleanup when V2 is enabled but V1 is disabled, leaving orphaned permissions/resources/policies. This is the same inconsistent feature-flag guarding problem described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Multiple ClientPermissionEvaluator methods in ClientPermissionsV2 throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"), so any remaining V1-era call path would produce an HTTP 500 instead of a deny decision in the authorization component

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds `ClientPermissionsV2` where multiple `ClientPermissionEvaluator`/`ClientPermissions` methods (e.g., `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, various `*Permission(...)` methods) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. This creates a concrete risk that any code path still invoking those methods while using the V2 implementation will crash rather than return an authorization decision. The diff even shows an existing call site that would be problematic *if* it is wired to V2: in `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, on `ClientRemovedEvent` it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false);`, which would throw if `clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`. However, the diff does not show how `management(...)` selects V1 vs V2, so an actual HTTP 500 is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: getClientsWithPermission iterates type-Clients resources and adds resource names to the result, so the all-clients sentinel resource name can be mixed into the set of client ids, causing callers that use the set as client ids to misbehave
matched_golden_ids: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core problem: getClientsWithPermission is iterating the type-level "Clients" resource(s) and returning resource names, which are not actual client IDs. This means the result can include the all-clients/type sentinel resource name and be used incorrectly as client IDs by callers (e.g., realm.getClientById), leading to misbehavior/nulls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is a private, never-called dead helper with stale V1 token-exchange-era attribute wiring; should be removed

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, the private helper `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff. Related token-exchange methods (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, etc.) all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, so this helper is effectively dead code and can be removed as cleanup. The claim about it being “stale V1 token-exchange-era wiring” isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the unused/dead-helper aspect is.
